newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares marked down as no post-Fed rush.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares marked down as no post-Fed rush.

text.p: Leading Russian shares eased on Thursday as domestic operators were forced to mark down prices they had raised the previous day, traders said.

"Investors do not want to buy at the peak," UFG trader Maxim Perlin said, explaining Western investors had not raided the market, foiling local expectations, after the U.S. Federal Reserve decided this week not to raise interest rates.
Traders saw the market quiet over the next week as Western investors mulled prices they still considered high, but said sellers were drying up as prices fell.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index fell 1.9 percent to 359.04 from 365.96 on Wednesday.

Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS metals group shares bucked the general easing on expectations of an American Depositary Receipt issue to allow foreign trade. Norilsk shares closed at $7.49 after $7.22 on Wednesday.
Utilities were the most-traded sector but results varied.
National power utility UES EESR.RTS, the turnover leader on $8.5 million, more than four times its closest competitor, ticked up to $0.3180 from $0.3150.
Utility Sverdlovenergo SVER.RTS fell to $0.679 from $0.720 and Novosibirskenergo NVNG.RTS utility rose to about $7.00 from $6.45.

Creditanstalt senior trader Andrei Galperin said leading shares would be quiet for a couple of weeks as investors mulled current prices though less liquid second-tier shares were seeing But Alfa Capital trader Dmitry Lobanov said the second tier had been shaken by the freezing of MinFin bonds on Thursday. "(The second tier) will hold for another week, but if the blue chips go down, this market will follow them," he said.
Perlin said prices fell on Thursday mostly because expectations of local dealers were not met.
"When it became clear the demand they had expected from New York did not appear, everything went down," he said.
